title: Spend governor: per-tenant adaptive headroom with GPU-family affinity and staged model variant degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a tenant-aware spend governor that enforces per-tenant soft budget headroom while preferring GPU families and gracefully degrading to cheaper model variants. The controller should dynamically adjust routing decisions across region/tier/instance-class and perform staged fallback: first shift to lower-cost GPU family (if compatible), then route to quantized or smaller model variants, and only finally throttle or queue when headroom is exhausted. This ticket covers design, implementation of the routing hook, integration with spend windows, runtime simulation tests, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Routing controller enforces per-tenant headroom percentage configurable via tenant profile
GPU-family affinity respected: prefer higher-performance GPUs up to headroom, fallback to cheaper GPU families when cost threshold crossed
Model-variant degradation flow implemented: variant mappings defined and routable by policy (e.g., vXL -> vL-quant -> vM) and fallback preserves schema/compatibility
Spot vs on-demand decisions incorporate eviction-risk smoothing: avoid flapping due to short-term spot price spikes
Integration tests simulating 3 tenants with different budgets show expected routing behavior across 30-day spend window
Latency and quality SLOs measured during canary (1% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on regression
Dashboards: per-tenant cost, instance-class allocation, eviction-rate, variant-shift counts, and token cost breakdown available
Docs/Runbook updated explaining configuration knobs, rollout steps, and recovery actions
discussion: 2025-03-04 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff. Problem: tenants hitting unexpected spend bursts leading to overage or emergency throttles. Goal: graceful degradation path that preserves SLOs and reduces cost without an abrupt user-visible outage.

2025-03-05 - Liam Chen: Drafted controller design. Key idea: maintain short-term headroom buffer (default 15%) per tenant, computed from rolling 30-day spend and projected velocity. Implement three-tier decision: preferred GPU family, compatible fallback GPU families, then model variants. Added eviction smoothing window (60s) to avoid reactive spot oscillation.

2025-03-06 - Design review (Priya Rao): Request to validate model-variant compatibility matrix and to include a fallback quality budget (max BLEU/embedding-drift thresholds). Also suggested exposing a tenant opt-out flag for aggressive variant degrading.

2025-03-07 - Security (Omar Williams): No PCI/PHI expansion but asked for audit events when tenant headroom enforcement changes routing; will be covered via existing audit pipeline. Flagged release for post-deploy audit checks.

2025-03-08 - Engineering (Liam Chen): Implemented prototype routing hook and a simulator to replay historical tenant traffic. Initial simulation shows 28% cost reduction for noisy tenant when enabling GPU-family fallback, with P95 latency increase under 12% for the first fallback. Added canary plan to incrementally enable for low-risk tenants first.

2025-03-09 - PM (Riley Thompson): Approved canary cohort and communication plan. Agreed on metrics for rollback: increased error rate >1% absolute, P95 latency >20% change, or quality regression above threshold for two consecutive hours.

2025-03-10 - QA (Nora Patel): Started load tests against staging with injected spot-eviction events. Found an edge case where request pinning to KV cache prevented automatic variant routing; created follow-up ENG-582318 to add cache-eviction hints with routing decisions.
